Describe cryptographic hardware and the methods of its implementation.

Cryptographic hardware is a type of hardware that is specialized for cryptohraphic operations which may be strenuous for the CPU. It provides support for symmetric ciphers (shifts, S-Box, operations in \(GF(2^8)\), etc.) and asymmetric ciphers (operations in \(GF(p)\), elliptic curve operations, modular exponentiation, etc.). Cryptographic hardware can be implemented as follows:
- dedicated cryptographic core of the CPU,
- cryptographic coprocessor connected via a bus.

Describe the origin of the power analysis side-channel attack.

The power consumption of a device depends on the degree of activity of its logical circuits which are typically made up of CMOS transistors. State transitions of a CMOS transistor increase the power consumption of the device linking the power consumption to the operations and values which are processed on the device as activity on its logical circuits triggers these transitions.
Metadata původního zdroje pro kartu 1740392746851: zelený příznak autora: duplicita; v původním balíčku pozastavená karta.
Describe the common approach for power analysis side-channel attacks.
Power analysis side-channel attacks usually use the following infrastructure:
- **oscilloscope** - measures the power consumption of the cryptographic device and provides the data to the computer,
- **computer** - controls the computations carried out by the cryptographic device and analyses data from the oscilloscope.
Describe the properties of a power consumption signal.
Power consumption signal consists of the following properties:\[P_\text{total}(t) = P_\text{op}(t) + P_\text{data}(t) + P_\text{el. noise}(t) + P_\text{const} (t),\]where:
- \(P_\text{el. noise}\) is electronic noise independent of both operations and data,
Only \(P_\text{op}\) and \(P_\text{data}\) are exploitable by power analysis attacks. This can be expressed as
- \(P_\text{sw. noise}\) is switching noise which is dependent on both operations and data but not exploitable.
\[P_\text{total}(t) = P_\text{exp}(t) + P_\text{sw. noise}(t) + P_\text{el. noise}(t) + P_\text{const}(t).\]
Metadata původního zdroje pro kartu 1740394206820: zelený příznak autora: duplicita; v původním balíčku pozastavená karta.
Describe the types of power analysis side-channel attacks.
Power analysis side-channel attacks can be categorized as follows:
- **simple power analysis** - single trace analysed along the time axis,
- **differential power analysis** - multiple traces analysed at the same fixed points in time.
Metadata původního zdroje pro kartu 1740394227584: zelený příznak autora: duplicita; v původním balíčku pozastavená karta.
Describe the process of differential power analysis.
Differential power analysis consists of the following phases:
- choose an intermediate value \(v = f(d, k)\) which depends on known input data \(d\) and an unknown partial key (the partial key must be short enough to be guessable);
- measure power traces \(t_i\) while encrypting different samples of data \(d_i\);
- build a matrix of hypothetical intermediate values \(v_{ij}\) for each of the possible keys \(k\) and used data samples \(d\);
- using a power consumption model, compute the matrix \(h_{ij}\) of hypothetical power consumption;
- statistically evaluate which hypothetical key best matches the measued power traces.
Metadata původního zdroje pro kartu 1740395308189: zelený příznak autora: duplicita; v původním balíčku pozastavená karta.
Describe the power consumption models used in differential power analysis.
Differential power analysis uses the following power consumption models:
- **single bit model** - the power consumption depends on a single bit of the intermediate value,
- **haming weight **- the power consumption depends on the number of set bits in the intermediate value,
- **hamming distance** - the power consumption depends on the number of differing bits between the current and the previous intermediate value.
Describe the difference between correlation power analysis (CPA) and differential power analysis (DPA).
Both correlation power analysis (CPA) and differential power analysis (DPA) are types of power analysis side-channel attacks but they differ in the following characteristics:
compares power traces with a theoretical model of power consumption |
compares power traces with differing keys or data |
typically uses Pearson's correlation coefficient  | typically uses difference of means or distance of means |
typically requires a smaller number of power traces |
typically requires a larger number of power traces
Describe the statistical evaluation in differential power analysis (DPA).
Statistical evaluation in differential power analysis (DPA) requires the following data:
- measured traces of power consumption paired to the plaintexts.
It starts off with a matrix of traces \(\mathbf T\) where:
- the row index specifies a trace,
- the column index specifies a point in time,
- the element is the byte of a trace at a given point in time.

Now suppose we are targetting the first byte of the key using an intermediate value\[v_{i, j} = \texttt{SBox}(d_i^{(0)} \oplus k_j^{(0)}),\]where \(d_i^{(0)}\) is the first byte of the \(i\)-th plaintext and \(k_j^{(0)}\) is the \(j\)-th possible value of the first byte of a key. This yields the matrix of hypothetical intermediate \(\mathbf V\) values where:
- the row index specifies a plaintext,
- the column index specifies a possible value of the first byte of the key,
- the element is the intermediate value \(v_{i, j}\).

Next, by applying a model of power consumption on \(\mathbf V\) we receive the matrix of hypothetical power consumption \(\mathbf H\). The dimensions of this matrix as well as the meaning of its columns and rows remains the same. Thereafter, we construct a correlation matrix \(\mathbf R\) of matrices \(\mathbf T\) and \(\mathbf H\) where:
- the row index specifies a possible value of the first byte of the key,
- the column index speficies a point in time.
- the element is the correlation between the measured power consumption and the hypothetical power consumption.

The last step is to identify the largest absolute value in the matrix. The larger the absolute value the stronger the correlation meaning a higher probability of the key byte hypothesis being correct.

Side-channel attack is typically a passive non-invasive attack. It exploits information emitted by the target which is typically not a part of its main function. Side-channels typically abuse the weaknesses of:
- **algorithms** - may leak information in a suitable format (square-and-multiply),
- **architectures** - influence the timing and order of operations (Meltdown, Spectre),
- **technologies** - influence power consumption or emitted electromagnetic field.

Describe the types of side-channel attacks.
- **timing **- duration of an operation depends on secret data (array comparison attack),
- **error** - error code depends on secret data (padding oracle),
- **power** - power consumption depends on secret data (simple power analysis, differential power analysis),
- **electromagnetic** - emitted electromagnetic field depends on secret data (TEMPEST).

Describe the power side-channel attack on square and multiply.

Power side-channel attack on square and multiply works by measuring the power consumption of the target device. The multiplication branch in square-and-multiply executes only if the bit at the given position in the exponent is set to 1. Therefore, the bits of the exponent are revealed through spikes in the power consumption of the device.
Describe the simple power analysis (SPA) side-channel attack on the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES).

Simple power analysis (SPA) side-channel attack on the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) targets the expanded key rather than the main encryption key. This is because the Hamming weights of the main key provide too little information. The expanded key can be divided into 4 parts each consisting of 5 bytes. The main idea is that these parts deterministically influence each other and these relations can be expressed using algebraic equations. Given a part \(P_i\) we can compute:
- 4 bytes of \(P_{i + 1}\) and 1 \(\texttt{SubBytes}\) result used in \(P_{i + 1}\),
- 3 bytes of \(P_{i - 1}\) and 1 \(\texttt{SubBytes}\) result used in \(P_{i - 1}\),
- 2 bytes of \(P_{i - 2}\) and 1 \(\texttt{SubBytes}\) result used in \(P_{i - 2}\),
- 1 byte of \(P_{i-3}\) and 1 \(\texttt{SubBytes}\) result used in \(P_{i-3}\).
Including the 5 bytes of \(P_i\), this yields 22 bytes in total. The attack is then carried out as follows:
- measure the Hamming weight of all of the 22 bytes above;
- choose 5 bytes to be plugged as \(P_i\) that match the measured Hamming weights;
- compute the rest of the related bytes and check if their Hamming weights match the measured Hamming weights;
- if they all match, remember them as key candidates.

This process then gets repeated for all of the possible combinations of the 5 bytes. The more Hamming weights of the parts of the key expansion we are able to measure, the more we will be able to decrease the possible keyspace.

It is important to realize that there are multiple values of a byte that have a given Hamming weight (e.g. for Hamming weight of 1, we have 8 possible values). Inaccuracies in the measurement of the Hamming weights will further increase the key space.

Describe the key expansion in the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES).

Suppose 32 bit words and the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) cipher with key \(k\) consisting of \(N_k\) words. Next, suppose an array of words \(w\). First, copy \(k\) into \(w\) starting from its beginning. As a result, the elements \(w[0], \dots, w[N_k - 1]\) will be occupied. Then, \(w[i]\) can be computed as follows:

- Select the word at \(w[i - N_k]\). If \(|i|_{N_k} = 0\) apply \(\texttt{RotWord}\) (rotation of its bytes), \(\texttt{SubWord}\) (substitution of its bytes), and \(\texttt{Rcon}\) (multiplication of its bytes using a constant).
- Select the word at \(w[i - 1]\). If \(N_k > 6\) and \(|i|_{N_k} = 4\) apply \(\texttt{SubWord}\) (substitution of its bytes).
- XOR both selected words and store the result at \(w[i]\).

Describe the influence of electronic noise on the power consumption signal.

The electronic noise component \(P_\text{el. noise}\) of the power consumption signal is measured by repeating the same operation with the same data. It is approximated using the normal distribution. Therefore, electronic noise can be decreased by averaging the traces.
Describe the influence of data on the power consumption signal.

The data-dependent component \(P_\text{data}\) of the power consumption signal is measured by repeating a single operation with different data. It is usually approximated using the normal distribution. This stems from the fact that microcontrollers typically leak hamming weights of internal data because they precharge their buses to either a logical 1 or 0 to eliminate electronic noise (circuit floating). Assuming uniformly distrbuted data, hamming weights can be modelled using the binomial distrubution. However, by applying a model of electronic noise, their distribution converges to the normal distribution.

In order to precharge their busses, microcontrollers can use the following components which have characteristic impact on the leakage \(l\) of the internal data \(d\) as the value of the signal changes:
- **pullup resistors** - maintain a logical 1, therefore\[l = \operatorname{hw}(\overline d),\]
where \(\operatorname{hw}(d)\) is the hamming weight taken from the binary form of \(d\).

Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) compares the level of the desired signal to the level of noise:\[\text{SNR} = \frac{\operatorname{var} (\text{signal})}{\operatorname{var}(\text{noise})} = \frac{\operatorname{var} P_\text{exp}}{\operatorname{var}(P_\text{sw. noise} + P_\text{el. noise})}.\]Higher SNR values indicate a better ratio of \(P_\text{exp}\) to overall noise. This can be used to optimize power analysis by only analysing time intervals with high SNR.
Describe the compression of traces in a power analysis attack.

The compression of traces in a power analysis attack aims reduce the computational complexity of the attack. Measured traces typically contain redundancies which can be decreased using the following methods of compression:
- **maximum extraction** - only keep intervals with high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR),
- **integration** - sum up raw values, absolute values, or squares of traces from an interval.
Describe hiding in the context of power side-channels.

Hiding is a power side-channel countermeasure that attempts to minimize the exploitable component \(P_\text{exp}\) of the power consumption signal therefore minimizing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Describe hiding in time in the context of power side-channels.

Hiding in time is an approach to the hiding power-side channel countermeasure. Because differential power analysis (DPA) requires traces to be aligned, hiding in time deliberatly misaligns them. This is done by performing operations at different points in time for every encryption. There are two main approaches to hiding in time:
- **insertion of dummy operations** - random clock cycles or \(\texttt{nop}\)s before, during, and after encryption;
- **shuffling** - randomizing the sequence of operations (e.g. S-Box lookups can be done in any order).
- **hardware** - dummy clock cycles (cycles in which dummy operations are performed), skipping of clock pulses, changing of clock frequencies, switching between multiple clocks.
Describe hiding in amplitude in the context of power side-channels.

Hiding in time is an approach to the hiding power-side channel countermeasure. It works by manipulating the power consumption signal to randomize power consumption of all operations. There are two main approaches to hiding in amplitude:
- **minimizing the exploitabe component** (\(\operatorname{var} P_\text{exp} \to 0\)) - all operations consume the same amount of power for any data;
- **maximizing noise **(\(\operatorname{var} (P_\text{sw. noise} + P_\text{el. noise}) \to \infty\)) - random switching dominates power consumption.
- **software** - choosing instructions with low leakage, avoiding data-dependent branching and memory adressing, paralelization;
Describe the influence of operations on the power consumption signal.

The operation-dependent component \(P_\text{op}\) of the power consumption signal is measured by repeating different operations with the same data. It is usually aproximated using the normal distribution; however, a larger amount of samles is required to eliminate electronic noise. Although often assumed, in practice \(P_\text{op}\) and \(P_\text{data}\) are rarely independent.
Describe attacks on hiding in the context of power side-channels.
Methods of attacking the hiding countermeasure in power side-channel attacks differ based on the type of hiding used. Hiding in time can be attacked using:
- **trace realignment** - computing cross-correlation to discover prominent features and using them to realign the traces,
- **trace integration** - adding the trace to itself shifted along the time axis may bring traces into alignment.
